senses.gloss: m.(b. h. חֶרֶשׂ; חרס to be rough; to scrape)

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 3:1">Kel. III, 1</cite> (ed. Dehr. <cite ref="H01777"><he>חרש</he></cite>); a. v. fr.—

Ib. 4 היה בה ח׳ if there remained of it a (sound) piece large enough to contain &c.—Tanḥ. Sh’laḥ. 1 (ref. to חֶרֶשׁ, Josh. II, 1) קרי ביה ח׳ read it ḥeres (with earthware, in the disguise of potters); Num. R. s. 16, beg. חרשׂ; a. fr.—Esp. (v. חַסְפָּא) potsherd.

Y. Ned. I, 37ᵃ top; Y. Naz. I, beg. 51ᵃ והתני … לא חספא did not Bar K. say, ḥeres is a substitute for ḥerem (חֵרֶם)? now, does not this mean a sherd (which has no reference to anything forbidden either as sacred or as doomed to destruction)?; v. next w.—Pl. חֲרָסִים, חֲרָסִין.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 9:5">Ib. IX, 5</cite> (Ar. <cite ref="H01789"><he>חֲרָשִׂין</he></cite>); a. e.—

<cite ref="Chagigah 13b:2">Ḥag. 13ᵇ</cite> (expl. <he>בזק</he>, <cite ref="Ezekiel 1:14">Ez. I, 14</cite>) <he>כאור … מבין הח׳</he> like the flames from between the perforated earthen pieces (used in smelting gold).
